exercise.name: Band Twist (Down-Up)

reference.title: Band twist (down up)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk rotation with a diagonal arm pull)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you drive the band up and across, breathe in as the arms return down to the anchor.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 1.5 s back down

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of losing control of the return (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: step farther from the anchor for more tension
prescription.progression: Stronger band, slower return, half-kneeling version for more trunk control

cues.text: Stand side-on to the anchor, band tied low on the upright. Feet a little wider than the hips; sit into a quarter squat, turn toward the anchor and hold the handle with both hands low beside the outside of the near thigh.
Breathe out and drive the band up and across the body to above the far shoulder, standing up and turning the hips and ribs together, arms long.
Brief pause high; ribs down, shoulders away from the ears, feet planted.
Let the arms come back down to the anchor slowly, sitting back into the quarter squat and turning back as one piece.
Chest up at the bottom, then drive up again. Turn around to train the other side.

mistakes.fix: Drive with the legs and turn the hips and ribs together; the arms stay long and guide the band.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Sit the hips back and keep the chest up; bend the knees rather than the spine.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band yank the arms back down
Arching back and shrugging at the top
mistakes.fix: Finish with the ribs down and the shoulders low; stop at about head height.

kinematics.norm: Ribs and hips turn together from facing the anchor to facing away; mostly thoracic and hip rotation (clinical opinion; end-range twisting under flexion is the concern, Marshall and McGill 2010)
Diagonal from low beside the near thigh to above the far shoulder (clinical opinion)
Quarter squat at the bottom, nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #25201, Band twist (down up), video (movement reference)
Torso-twist exercise with elastic resistance vs a training machine: core muscle EMG (Scientifica 2015:403068; PubMed 26557405)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)
Marshall and McGill 2010, the role of axial torque in disc herniation (Clin Biomech 25:6-9), porcine model

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the band and the anchor before each set: a band that slips or snaps can hit you, and the hands finish near the face.
Keep the range comfortable and turn the hips with the ribs; avoid a forceful end-range twist with a rounded back (Marshall and McGill 2010).
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: smaller turn, or a half-kneeling chop.
Shoulder discomfort: finish at chest height instead of above the shoulder.
regressions: Lighter band or stand closer to the anchor.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the trunk up and across against the band (oblique pair across the trunk). In elastic-band torso twists the external oblique reached about 54-77% MVC (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the trunk up and across against the band (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.core: Transversus and rectus abdominis brace the trunk and stop the low back arching at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Raise the long arms up and across (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Raise the long arms up and across (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drive the hips up out of the quarter squat and help turn the pelvis (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drive the hips up out of the quarter squat and help turn the pelvis (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Straighten the knees as you stand up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Straighten the knees as you stand up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Turn and steady the pelvis over the planted feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Turn and steady the pelvis over the planted feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the chest up in the low start (erector spinae about 32-50% MVC in torso twists, Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the chest up in the low start (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Support the shoulder blade as the arms rise (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Support the shoulder blade as the arms rise (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Turns the shoulder blade up as the arms rise (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Turns the shoulder blade up as the arms rise (clinical opinion).
